booth.welcome.3.t: Good morrow, good people. If you have money on this, you are not alone. Nor wise.

booth.welcome.8.t: Every bench is taken. Some of them twice… By men who paid but once, by my faith.

booth.venue.smithfield.2.t: The knights rode out from the Tower this morning… Each led by a lady, on a silver chain.

booth.venue.smithfield.5.t: Smithfield is also where they burn men for heresy. The King bids you enjoy the jousting.

booth.venue.inglevert.1.t: At Saint-Inglevert a knight touches a shield to choose: the shield of peace… Or the shield of war.

booth.venue.inglevert.3.t: The holders are Boucicaut, de Roye and Sempy. They have pitched their pavilions… And mean to bide.

booth.venue.leon.1.t: Suero de Quiñones has sworn to break three hundred lances here, and wears an iron collar every Thursday for his lady.

booth.venue.leon.4.t: One knight at Órbigo took a point through the eye and died upon the field. Yet still they came. They kept coming.

booth.venue.bruges.1.t: There is a dwarf with an hourglass. When the sand has run… The course is over.

booth.venue.nuremberg.1.t: German harness for the Stechen: the helm bolted to the breastplate. A man sees out… Only by leaning forward.

booth.mode.planken.0.t: Hear the reckoning: a touch, one. A lance broken, two. Broken upon the helm… Three.

booth.mode.tiptoft.1.t: By Tiptoft's rule, a spear broken on the body is one, on the helm two… And bearing your man down, three.

booth.mode.tiptoft.3.t: Strike the horse under these rules, and the prize is forfeit. No appeal. No excuse.

booth.mode.castile.1.t: Four courses only. Only a lance splintered with the point shall count. Broken crosswise… Nothing.

booth.mode.sudden.1.t: One clean break ends it. Touches count for nothing. Nerves count for everything.

booth.mode.judged.1.t: A point for a steady lance, a point for raising it in good time, and one taken off for leaving it low.

booth.mode.bridge.1.t: Win two bouts and the bridge is held. The horse is granted no fresh pair of legs for the second.

booth.mode.gestech.1.t: Break the lance, or bear the man down. That is the whole of the Gestech.

booth.mode.rennen.1.t: The mark is the tall shield upon the breast. Strike it square, and it springs away. Nothing else counts.

booth.knight.clifford.0.t: Sir Thomas Clifford, an English knight of the old school. Mail… And opinions.

booth.knight.renaud.0.t: Renaud de Roye, one of the three holders at Saint-Inglevert. Swift… And he knows it well.

booth.knight.boucicaut.1.t: Boucicaut. Marshal of France one day, if no man kills him first. No man has managed it.

booth.knight.lalaing.1.t: Lalaing held a pavilion by a fountain at Chalon a twelvemonth, against all comers. The Fountain of Tears.

booth.knight.quinones.1.t: Three hundred lances, he swore. He is counting. So are the carpenters.

booth.knight.freydal.1.t: Freydal, in German harness — the Stechzeug. Bolted, doubled… Near enough a wall.

booth.knight.palman.0.t: Palman of Styria. He captained the German men for the King of Serbia. He does not joust for sport.

booth.knight.ulrich.1.t: They say Ulrich cut off his own finger and sent it to his lady. She was not so moved as he had hoped.

booth.knight.blackprince.1.t: The Prince has the finest seat in Christendom… And the worst temper. Both will be on show.

booth.knight.field.0.t: A new man upon the roll. New to most of us.

booth.knight.field.3.t: Not old arms, his. Bought, some say.

booth.you.new.1.t: First time in the lists for this one. Mark the lance… It shakes a little.

booth.you.new.3.t: No record, no name, no debts as yet. Give it an afternoon.

booth.you.rising.0.t: This one begins to be talked of. In taverns. Favourably, for the most part.

booth.you.known.0.t: A knight whose name the heralds no longer have to spell.

booth.you.champion.1.t: Honours on the roll, and the King knows the name. That is a perilous thing… To be known to the King.

booth.grudge.1.t: There is old quarrel here. The last meeting went the other way… And no man has forgotten it.

booth.revenge.0.t: Our man won the last time they met. The other has not ceased to speak of it.

booth.arms.0.t: Mark the arms upon the shield, plain enough to read at a gallop.

booth.arms.3.t: The heralds will be painting both shields upon the roll tonight… One way or the other.

booth.horse.destrier.2.t: The destrier is heavy in the shock. The lance goes where the horse goes… And the horse goes through.

booth.horse.courser.2.t: A courser brings speed to the stroke. Whether the rider can keep pace is another matter.

booth.horse.rouncey.2.t: Light in the shock, the rouncey… But it never tires, and it never takes fright.

booth.stakes.final.1.t: The last day of the event. Win here, and the heralds cry your name in the hall tonight.

booth.stakes.first.0.t: The first day of a first season. Some man in this field is about to learn something.

booth.stakes.early.0.t: An early round. Lose here… And you are a spectator with an excellent seat.

booth.ready.0.t: Lances up. Visors down. This is the quiet hour.

booth.ready.2.t: Both at their marks. The squires stand back.

booth.ready.4.t: The commons hush. Even the pie man holds his tongue.

booth.ready.6.t: The flag is raised. Both knights… Waiting on it.

booth.away.4.t: Off they go, down the lists!

booth.away.6.t: They are off. Mark the points!

booth.away.7.t: Away… And the stands are up!

booth.charge.aim.0.t: He has his eye upon the helm.

booth.charge.aim.2.t: Low and true at the shield.

booth.after.breakYou.3.t: A clean break for our man. Square upon the shield.

booth.after.breakYou.7.t: Splinters to the rail. That one will be picked out of the commons for a week.

booth.after.breakYou.9.t: Two to the cheque, or near enough. The heralds are writing.

booth.after.breakHim.3.t: He breaks his lance. A good, honest stroke.

booth.after.breakHim.6.t: A broken lance against. The stands go quiet upon this side.

booth.after.bothBreak.3.t: Two lances in pieces. The carpenters will be busy tonight.

booth.after.bothBreak.6.t: Splinters everywhere. The heralds will need a second roll.

booth.after.helmYou.4.t: The helm rang like a church bell. A lady in the gallery crossed herself.

booth.after.helmYou.6.t: A stroke for the roll of arms. The heralds will be dining out on that one.

booth.after.helmHim.2.t: Upon the helm, against. That will have been loud within.

booth.after.helmHim.5.t: A blow upon the helm… And our man still in the saddle. That is iron and stubbornness.

booth.after.glanceYou.2.t: A touch, and it skids away. Too flat at the meeting.

booth.after.glanceYou.5.t: The point met the shield and slid. An attaint… No more.

booth.after.glanceHim.2.t: His point glances away. Good shield work.

booth.after.attaint.2.t: A touch that holds. The lance did not break.

booth.after.attaint.5.t: An attaint. The judges hold the flag level. A touch… No more.

booth.after.missYou.2.t: Nothing for our man. The point went by.

booth.after.missYou.5.t: Wide. A good yard of air. The commons let him know it.

booth.after.missHim.2.t: He misses. A clean pass… And nothing to show.

booth.after.missHim.5.t: A miss against. That costs him nothing on the cheque… And a great deal in the stands.

booth.after.bothMiss.3.t: They passed each other like strangers in a cloister.

booth.after.bothMiss.6.t: The commons are whistling. They did not pay to watch two men go for a canter.

booth.after.unhorseYou.3.t: Borne to the ground. Over the cantle… And the horse runs on without him.

booth.after.unhorseYou.6.t: The squires are running. The marshal's men are running. He is going nowhere.

booth.after.unhorseHim.1.t: Our man is upon the sand.

booth.after.unhorseHim.3.t: Borne down. A great stroke against… And the stands have gone very quiet.

booth.after.tilt.3.t: He struck the tilt. Points off… And a carpenter somewhere sighs.

booth.after.foul.3.t: A stroke upon the horse. The judges raise the red flag. The King's grace likes it not.

booth.after.injuryYou.1.t: The surgeon is watching closely. He has his bag open.

booth.after.injuryHim.1.t: His squires hold him in the saddle. That is no good sign.

booth.score.planken.0.t: The heralds have their sums. The cheque is close.

booth.score.planken.2.t: Every line on that cheque is a lance some man did not wish to lose.

booth.score.tiptoft.0.t: Under Tiptoft that is one for the body. Nothing for a touch. The Earl was not sentimental.

booth.score.tiptoft.2.t: Watch the sight of the helm. Three strokes there take the prize under Tiptoft… Whatever the count.

booth.score.judged.0.t: The judges add their marks: a steady lance, and the lance raised in good time.

booth.score.sudden.0.t: Still no lance broken, so still no winner. Sudden death… Waits.

booth.score.castile.0.t: Only a splintered lance counts under the Statutes. A crosswise break is nothing.

booth.score.gestech.0.t: In the Gestech, the break is what counts… And the fall counts most.

booth.score.rennen.0.t: Only the shield counts in the Rennen. Strike it square… And up it springs.

booth.score.bridge.0.t: The bridge keeps its own tally. Bouts won… Bouts lost.

booth.momentum.comeback.1.t: What a turn! An hour since, the bookmakers were laughing.

booth.momentum.comeback.3.t: The stands have changed sides. Hark to them.

booth.momentum.collapse.0.t: He had it… And now it slips. The lead is gone.

booth.momentum.streakYou.0.t: Another! That is three courses running.

booth.momentum.streakHim.0.t: Him again. He has the measure of it.

booth.momentum.lastCourse.0.t: The last course. Everything upon it.

booth.momentum.lastCourse.3.t: One more course and it is decided… Unless God or the barrier has a say.

booth.momentum.lastCourse.4.t: The final course of the match. Hark to the stands.

booth.momentum.extra.0.t: Level after the courses. One more… To settle it.

booth.momentum.runawayHim.0.t: He is running away with it.

booth.result.win.1.t: The judges agree, the stands agree, and the King's grace is applauding. That is a win, by my faith.

booth.result.win.4.t: Favours from the gallery, caps in the air… And some man's purse much lighter.

booth.result.win.6.t: The heralds will cry that name in the hall tonight, and the ladies will pretend not to listen.

booth.result.loss.1.t: A loss… But a brave one. The stands are kinder than the cheque.

booth.result.loss.4.t: He rides off with his head up. That is worth something. Not a purse. Something.

booth.result.draw.1.t: Neither man beaten. Both will claim it in the tavern.

booth.result.firstWin.1.t: Remember the day. Some man will carve it upon a tomb one day.

booth.result.rankUp.0.t: The heralds will raise him upon the roll for that. A rank higher.

booth.result.champion.1.t: A champion. The King's grace will want a word. Let us hope it is a kind one.

booth.celebrate.stump.0.t: He holds the broken stump up to the stands.

booth.celebrate.salute.0.t: A bow, and the lance raised to the royal box.

booth.celebrate.fists.0.t: Up in the stirrups, both fists in the air!

booth.celebrate.helm.0.t: The helm comes off… And he waves it.

booth.celebrate.point.0.t: He points at the commons… And cups an ear.

booth.celebrate.rear.0.t: The horse goes up! A pesade!

booth.celebrate.gallery.0.t: A slow ride along the gallery, arm raised to the ladies.

booth.celebrate.favour.0.t: A bow to a lady… And she throws him her ribbon.

booth.celebrate.nod.0.t: A nod of the head… To the better man.

booth.celebrate.slap.0.t: He slaps his own helm. He is ill pleased with himself.

booth.aftermath.down.0.t: He is not rising. The surgeon is running out.

booth.aftermath.up.0.t: He is on his feet. A hand from the squire… And he stands.

booth.aftermath.carried.0.t: They bear him from the field.

booth.filler.4.t: A word upon the coronel. Three blunt prongs, to catch upon the shield and break the lance… Not the man.

booth.filler.6.t: The vamplate is the steel disc on the lance that guards the hand. Without it you joust with nine fingers. Briefly.

booth.filler.11.t: For those just arriving: the lists are open, the ale is warm, and the King has not yet had any man arrested.

booth.filler.13.t: The heralds keep the cheque, a column of marks for each rider. No man argues with the cheque. They argue with heralds.

booth.filler.17.t: The squires do most of the work and get none of the credit. Like heralds.

booth.filler.19.t: The marshal's word is law in the lists. Outside the lists, the marshal owes me two shillings.

booth.filler.23.t: The barrier is called the tilt, which is why the whole sport is called tilting, which is why I have a place.

booth.filler.25.t: The French call this the joust of peace. The French have a sense of humour. It is hard to find.

booth.filler.29.t: A word to the commons: casting things at the knights is forbidden. Casting things at the heralds is merely discouraged.

booth.filler.33.t: The squire hands up a fresh lance. Fourteen feet of painted fir… And every man's hopes.

booth.filler.36.t: The judges confer. Three old men, one table… And the whole afternoon written on their faces.

booth.filler.38.t: The wind sits in the west, which matters to the archers… And to nobody else.

booth.history.0.t: At Smithfield in 1390, King Richard gave out his white hart badge. It was the first time it was seen.

booth.history.1.t: Sixty ladies led sixty knights through London on chains… To the Smithfield jousts.

booth.history.2.t: At Saint-Inglevert the holders hung two shields at their pavilions. Touch the shield of war… And the points were sharp.

booth.history.3.t: At the Passo Honroso, a hundred and sixty-six combats were fought before the vow was held complete.

booth.history.4.t: At the pas of the Golden Tree, the challengers came one by one, twenty-six of them, to face the Bastard of Burgundy.

booth.history.5.t: The Bastard of Burgundy was kicked by a horse at his own pas. The horse was not punished.

booth.history.6.t: Jacques de Lalaing kept the Fountain of Tears at Chalon a full twelvemonth, a challenge on the first of every month.

booth.history.7.t: Tiptoft's ordinances were set down at Windsor in May of 1466… For the King's jousts.

booth.history.8.t: At the Gesellenstechen it was the young men of the patrician houses who rode. The country nobility stayed at home… And sniffed.

booth.history.9.t: The German tournament societies barred men by ancestry. Four noble grandparents… Or you watched from the rail.

booth.history.10.t: Under the Bamberg rules of 1478, a cheat might lose his horse and harness… And be shamed before the ladies.

booth.history.11.t: At a pas d'armes, a knight who would not fight left his spurs. A lady without an escort left a glove.

booth.history.12.t: King René's book of the tournament: the king of arms cries three times… Before the ropes are cut.

booth.history.13.t: At the end of a tourney the ladies choose the knight of honour. The judges merely count.

booth.history.14.t: In the Rennen the shield is built to spring off when it is struck square. The crowd loves the sound.

booth.newbie.encourage.0.t: First time in the lists, this one. Nobody learns it in a day. Give him a few courses.

booth.newbie.encourage.1.t: Missed. No shame in it. Every knight here missed his first dozen.

booth.newbie.encourage.2.t: It's hard at first, this. The lance is heavy and the horse has opinions. It gets easier.

booth.newbie.encourage.3.t: Let him stay on the course a while longer. It'll come.

booth.newbie.encourage.4.t: He's learning. Watch the point, not the horse. That's the whole trick.

booth.newbie.encourage.5.t: Not bad for a beginner. Not good either. But not bad.

booth.newbie.encourage.6.t: Steady. The first ten courses are the worst. After that it's merely terrible.

booth.newbie.encourage.7.t: Lower the point sooner. He'll get there.

booth.newbie.better.0.t: There! That's closer. A few more and he'll be dangerous.

booth.newbie.firstHit.0.t: Good! He's getting it. I said he would.

booth.newbie.roast.0.t: Did he skip the training ground? He skipped the training ground.

booth.newbie.roast.1.t: There's a quintain behind the stables. It doesn't hit back. He might try it.

booth.newbie.roast.2.t: That was painful. For us. Imagine how he feels.

booth.newbie.roast.3.t: Somebody show this man the practice yard. Please.

booth.newbie.roast.4.t: He rode in here with no training. Bold. Wrong, but bold.

booth.newbie.roast.5.t: I've seen sacks of flour sit a horse better.

booth.newbie.roast.6.t: Beaten, and soundly. The training ground is free, my lord. So is shame.

booth.newbie.roast.7.t: Back to the quintain with him. It's very patient.

squire.cheer.start.0.t: The lance is true, my lord. Ride well.

squire.cheer.start.1.t: Gauntlets laced, my lord. Good luck.

squire.cheer.start.2.t: All is ready, my lord. Go and spoil his afternoon.

squire.cheer.start.3.t: Visor down, my lord. Your face is frightening the horse.

squire.cheer.miss.0.t: He was quick, my lord. Next time.

squire.cheer.miss.1.t: Air, my lord. It happens to the best of men.

squire.cheer.miss.2.t: No matter, my lord. Nobody saw. Everybody saw. No matter.

squire.cheer.miss.3.t: You were looking at his helm. I saw your head go up.

squire.cheer.behind.0.t: We are behind, my lord, but only by a lance.

squire.cheer.behind.1.t: One good course turns it, my lord.

squire.cheer.behind.2.t: Behind, my lord. My father said behind is where the brave live. He was usually behind.

squire.cheer.leading.0.t: You lead, my lord! The stands are with you.

squire.cheer.leading.1.t: Ahead on points, my lord. I could shout!

squire.cheer.leading.2.t: Don't smile yet, my lord. Smile at supper.

crowd.start.2.t: Look at the horses! Oh, look!

crowd.start.3.t: Is that the King? Is that the King?

crowd.start.4.t: Get your hat off, I cannot see!

crowd.start.6.t: Two to one the blue! Two to one!

crowd.start.7.t: Not like the old days. Look at them. Babies.

crowd.start.8.t: Ten crowns on the home man.

crowd.start.9.t: Which is he? The one with the feathers?

crowd.ready.2.t: Quiet, you, he is about to go!

crowd.ready.5.t: Lower the flag! Lower it! Lower... the flag.

crowd.ready.6.t: Last bets! Last bets on the course!

crowd.ready.8.t: Lord, have mercy on the both of them.

crowd.ready.9.t: I cannot look. Tell me when.

crowd.break.1.t: Did you see that? Did you see it?

crowd.break.4.t: That is how it is done!

crowd.break.7.t: That is my money, that is!

crowd.break.9.t: Mind the wood! There is wood coming!

crowd.helm.4.t: Is he dead? Is he dead?

crowd.helm.6.t: The sight! Right in the sight!

crowd.helm.7.t: Oh! Oh, I cannot bear it!

crowd.glance.4.t: Too gentle! You're not courting her!

crowd.attaint.1.t: Should have broken. That should have broken.

crowd.attaint.2.t: Break it! Break it next time!

crowd.miss.6.t: I paid good money for that!

crowd.miss.7.t: Lowered too soon. Always too soon.

crowd.bothMiss.3.t: I could do better with a broom!

crowd.unhorse.4.t: He fell off! He fell off!

crowd.unhorse.5.t: Get up! Get up and fight him!

crowd.unhorse.9.t: Over the cantle. Seen it a hundred times.

crowd.win.6.t: Pay up! Pay up, the lot of you!

crowd.loss.5.t: I knew it. I knew it all along.

crowd.gallery.3.t: My lady says you ride very well!

crowd.gallery.4.t: I'll have him! I'll have that one!

crowd.gallery.5.t: Leave him alone, he's spoken for!

crowd.idle.0.t: Three to one the stranger! Who'll take three to one?

crowd.idle.1.t: Evens, evens on the next course!

crowd.idle.2.t: A penny says he falls. A penny!

crowd.idle.3.t: Who had money on the blue? Hard luck.

crowd.idle.5.t: Get on with it! We're dying of age up here!

crowd.idle.6.t: In my day they had proper lances.

crowd.idle.7.t: Take your elbow out of my pie.

crowd.idle.8.t: I could do that. I could. Give me a horse.

crowd.idle.9.t: Who took my ale? Somebody took my... oh. There it is.

crowd.idle.12.t: When do they fall off again?

crowd.idle.13.t: Can I be a knight? Can I?

crowd.idle.14.t: That one's married. That one's married. That one should be.

crowd.idle.15.t: Look at the Queen's sleeves. Look at them.

crowd.idle.16.t: My Tom rode at Smithfield. Fell off twice. Still talks about it.

crowd.idle.18.t: Who's got the pies? Over here!

crowd.idle.20.t: Brothers, a little more charity, and a little less ale.

crowd.idle.21.t: They say the Duke paid for his horse with his wife's jewels.

crowd.idle.22.t: I hear his squire owes everybody money.

crowd.idle.23.t: Lances made of fir. Fir! Christmas wood.

crowd.idle.26.t: Whose dog is this? Get it off the sand!

crowd.largesse.2.t: A penny for the herald, and one for me!

crowd.honour.0.t: To the honour of the ladies!

crowd.honour.1.t: For the ladies! For the ladies!
